title: The Margosa Tree
text:
In a certain city there is a King, it is said. The King thought of
growing a Margosa tree without bitterness [in the fruit], so one day
he made proclamation accordingly by beat of tom-toms.

While two friends of one village were coming to seek a means of
subsistence they heard this sound of tom-toms. When they asked at the
hand of a tom-tom beater, "What is the sound of tom-toms for?" he said,
"What is it? His Majesty our King will give presents to any person
who should grow and give him a Margosa tree without bitterness." One
of the friends, saying, "I can [do it]," went to the royal palace.

"Canst thou grow and give me a Margosa tree without bitterness?" the
King asked.

"Yes, your Majesty," he said.

"What things dost thou want for it?" the King asked.

"I want monthly a hundred-weight of sugar and a large pot of cow's
butter," he said.

After that, the King asked, "Where wilt thou grow it?"

"I must grow it on the edge of a river," he said.

Having built and given him a house on the edge of the river, he gave
him a hundred-weight of sugar and a large pot of butter monthly.

Seven times in succession he planted seven trees. Seven times the
seven trees were washed away by the river.

During the time while he was there in that way, the other friend
having come, asked, "Where is the tree?"

Then the friend who had planted the tree says, "Either the King,
or I, or the river." [120]

The words that he said meant, "Either His Majesty the King will die;
if not, I shall die, because of no means of subsistence."

"Having cheated the King I get a living. When it is so, the foolish
King has been caught by my trick."

ある都に王がいたという。王は、実に苦みのないマルゴサ(センダン)の木を育てようと思いつき、ある日、太鼓を打ってその旨の触れを出させた。
ある村の二人の友が、暮らしの手だてを求めて来る途中、この太鼓の音を聞いた。太鼓打ちに「あの太鼓は何のためか」と尋ねると、太鼓打ちは言った。「何かと言うと、われらが王さまは、苦みのないマルゴサの木を育てて差し上げた者に褒美をくださるのだ」。友の一人は「わたしにはできる」と言って、王宮へ行った。
「そなたは苦みのないマルゴサの木を育ててわしに差し出せるか」と王が尋ねた。
「はい、陛下」と男は言った。
「そのために何が要る」と王が尋ねた。
「毎月、砂糖を百重量分と、牛の酪を大壺に一つ、いただきたく存じます」と男は言った。
そのあと王が尋ねた。「どこで育てるのか」
「川のほとりで育てねばなりません」と男は言った。
王は川のほとりに家を建てて与え、毎月、砂糖を百重量分と酪を大壺に一つ与えた。
男は続けて七度、七本の木を植えた。七度とも、七本の木は川に流された。
そうして暮らしているあいだに、もう一人の友が来て尋ねた。「木はどこだ」
すると木を植えたほうの友が言う。「王か、わたしか、川か、だ」 [120]
その言葉の意味はこうだった。「王さまが死ぬか、そうでなければ、暮らしの手だてを失ってわたしが死ぬか」
「王をだまして暮らしを立てている。そうしてみると、愚かな王はわたしの計略にかかったわけだ」
